source.title: Data-dependent Sample Complexity of Deep Neural Networks via Lipschitz Augmentation

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports Jacobian regularization results, but does not test any listed version: it does not test memorization of random labels, width beyond interpolation, the listed optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.gate_note: Section 8 reports test-error outcomes after adding Jacobian regularization. This finding concerns generalization but does not measure the training-to-test gap or a behavior named by the versions, so it is recorded under fits_no_version. Cited results from other studies are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study derives Jacobian-based generalization bounds and evaluates Jacobian regularization. Neither its proofs nor its experiments test V1–V8. Input or hidden-layer sensitivity is distinct from V7's magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive generalization bounds depending polynomially on hidden-layer and interlayer Jacobian norms and report preliminary improvements from Jacobian regularization.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments add Jacobian regularization to a WideResNet training objective; they do not implement the methods in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports results for low learning rate, no data augmentation, no BatchNorm, and LayerNorm settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Jacobian regularization reduced CIFAR-10 test error for WideResNet16 in the reported low-learning-rate, no-augmentation, and LayerNorm settings. Experiments used single runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularizing hidden-layer Jacobians can improve WideResNet16 test performance in some CIFAR-10 training settings.

record.problems: The experiments report results from a single run. The table is flattened in the supplied text, making some condition-to-value assignments unclear.
record.rows_left_out: Cited findings from prior work are not rows. The paper's complexity-measure depth comparison in Section G.2 measures scaling of a bound-related quantity rather than a training-test gap or any listed version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training under the same recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning and recovery recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.
Dropout effects across training-set sizes and configurations, including joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its association with measured generalization gaps, and its ranking against other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No version-specific verdict is warranted. A bound without explicit width dependence does not establish decreasing test error with width, and Jacobian regularization does not test magnitude-aware weight sharpness.

versions.untested_parts: Test error across widths beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, including the stated tuning and recovery conditions.
Large-batch versus small-batch performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects and its removal alongside weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the training-test gap.
Effects of removing memorized training examples.

rows.subject: WideResNet16
rows.operation_detail: Added a Jacobian regularization term to the training objective.

conditions.value: low learning rate, no data augmentation, no BatchNorm, and LayerNorm

rows.value: The authors report improvements in test error for all these settings; individual values are not assigned here because the table layout does not unambiguously associate every value with its condition.
rows.note: The authors state that Jacobian regularization improved test error in the low learning rate and no data augmentation settings, and in the LayerNorm setting. Table 1's flattened layout prevents reliable assignment of every displayed value to a specific condition.
rows.check: This aggregates several conditions and reports the study's own regularizer performance, so it should remain a fits_no_version finding rather than claim evidence. Table 1 identifies low-learning-rate test error as 5.98% without versus 5.46% with regularization, and no-augmentation error as 10.44% versus 8.25%. The normalization conditions should be separated: no normalization and LayerNorm are distinct. Figure 1 displays a complexity-measure distribution, not these test-error comparisons. The reported improvement is observable, but cannot establish any listed version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
